title: Async ranker: slice timebox and token capacity policy to reduce p99 latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint exhibits high tail latency when candidate sets are large or when a small number of requests contain very long contexts. Current continuous-batching approach increases throughput but allows a few requests to block microbatches for long windows, pushing p99/p999 above SLO.

Goal: Reduce p95/p99 latency for rerank while preserving overall throughput and not regressing top-line QPS. We will implement an asynchronous micro-slicing and timebox policy combined with per-request token budgets and soft timeouts so heavy requests do not amplify queueing for short requests. This ticket covers design, implementation, perf validation, and canary rollout on a dedicated cluster before platform-wide flip.

Scope: async worker pool for ranker evaluation, micro-slice timebox (configurable ms), per-request token_cap enforcement, speculative hedging for soft timeouts, KV prefetch prioritization for short-candidates, metrics/tracing, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for rerank endpoint decreases by at least 30% on replay of heavy candidate workload compared to baseline
no more than 5% regression in median latency or 3% regression in overall tokens/sec throughput on standard load tests
config knobs for slice_ms, token_cap, soft_timeout_ms are exposed in runtime and Console rollout UI
automated perf/regression dashboard added to Console with alert if tail latency increases > 20% after flip
canary rollout executed and rollback plan validated

comments: 2026-02-11 Marco Diaz: Spike results attached in Drive. Baseline replay of 10k heavy requests shows p99=980ms; median=48ms. Micro-slicing with 40ms window in the spike reduced p99 to 610ms but reduced tokens/sec by ~6%.

2026-02-13 Liang Chen: Reviewed design doc. Concern: prefetch may increase memory pressure if we prioritize short candidates aggressively. Recommend evict-first policy and configurable memory caps per worker.
2026-02-16 Priya Iyer: QA will create a replay harness based on production traces; need contract for synthetic trace format by EOD 2/18.

2026-02-22 Ben Cho: Proposed fallback policy: on soft_timeout we return current best scores and schedule a background refresh to update embeddings later. This keeps latency bounded for user-facing requests.
2026-03-02 Marco Diaz: Implementation PR opened (runtime#2784). Unit tests for token accounting added. Requesting review from Liang and Ben.
2026-03-06 Liang Chen: Left review comments on PR: edge-case when token_cap < single_candidate_tokens not handled. Suggested clamp+single-pass processing.

2026-03-09 SRE (Rosa Alvarez): Canary plan ready. We will route 5% traffic to rerank-canary in us-west for 48h then bump to 20% if no alerts. Alert conditions: p99 > baseline*1.2 or error rate > 0.5%.
2026-03-10 Marco Diaz: Merged runtime PR after addressing comments. Console PR pending. Starting canary tomorrow.
decisions: Adopt asynchronous worker pool with per-microbatch slice windows rather than strict synchronous batching to reduce queue head-of-line blocking
Enforce per-request token_cap; if a single request exceeds token_cap, process candidates in streaming chunks (clamped) to ensure progress
Implement soft_timeout (hedge) at 60% of slice_ms to trigger speculative evaluation on a warm fallback path rather than hard abort
Prioritize KV prefetch for candidates estimated to complete inside the current slice_ms window; deprioritize long candidates to next microbatch
Expose runtime knobs slice_ms, token_cap, soft_timeout_ms and a global emergency_disable flag in Console for rapid rollback
